references.text: Moses' sister had stood at a distance to see what would happen to him, and now she is sent to fetch his mother.
The sister had just suggested fetching a Hebrew nurse, and Pharaoh's daughter accepts the suggestion here.
The next verse shows the result of the young woman fetching the child's mother - she gets the child back to nurse it.
Jochebed is mentioned here as Moses' mother, the one the young woman was sent to fetch.
Jochebed is identified as the mother of Moses and Aaron, confirming who 'the child's mother' was.
The book of Hebrews mentions that Moses was hidden by his parents in faith, and this event is part of that account.
A theological parallel between a mother saving her son from death and a new 'mother' being taken into the faith after Christ's death.
Powerful theological contrast: Royal favor toward a young girl leads to death (Mark) or life/salvation (Exodus).
Typological parallel: A prophetic act where a child is returned to his mother to live (Elijah) versus saved from death (Moses).
